title: US Army Unit Conducts First In-House Drone Strike With 3D-Printed Munitions
key_facts: Soldiers of the US Army's 2nd Cavalry Regiment in Germany built and flew an attack drone using an Orqa MRM2-10 airframe and 3D-printed munitions they designed
Strike conducted in Bavaria; described as the first live kinetic drone strike by a conventional Army unit without contractor or outside unit support
Capt. Michael Bapp confirmed to Stars and Stripes; the bombs are called 'Dragoon bombs'
Payloads can be ball bearings or a shaped charge; drone range up to 12 miles
Army, Marine Corps and Navy are expanding drone and 3D-printing training and facilities
quote_evidence: Soldiers of the 2nd Cavalry Regiment launched an attack drone they assembled themselves from an Orqa MRM2-10 airframe, fitted with 3D-printed munitions they designed and printed on base.
The strike, conducted in Bavaria, represents the first time a conventional Army unit has executed a live kinetic drone strike without contractor or external unit support.
why_it_matters_hint: US soldiers are building their own armed drones, following lessons from Ukraine.
notes: Relayed from Stars and Stripes by a smaller site; strike date not given; 'first' is the unit's claim.
